Container.Name: nanoclaw-aio
Container.Overview:
NanoClaw AIO packages NanoClaw v2 as a Telegram-first Unraid container. You control the assistant from Telegram; NanoClaw stores runtime state under appdata and launches isolated helper containers from the paired jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent image when agent work needs to run.
This template is marked beta while the v2 runtime receives more real-world Unraid soak time. It requires the Docker socket, which gives the container host-level Docker control. Install only if you are comfortable trusting NanoClaw and this wrapper with that access.
First boot waits until TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and one Claude credential are configured. After startup, check the container logs for a PAIR_TELEGRAM_CODE and send that code to your Telegram bot to pair the main chat. Persistent databases, logs, groups, env files, and channel state live under /appdata.

Do not edit manually. - Rebuild NanoClaw AIO around upstream v2.0.63. - Add paired jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent:v2.0.63-agent.1 helper image. - Replace runtime git-fetch behavior with build-time Telegram adapter vendoring.

Container.ReadMe: Configure TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and at least one Claude credential, then start the container and watch the logs for PAIR_TELEGRAM_CODE. Send that code to your Telegram bot to pair the main chat. NanoClaw stores runtime state under /appdata and uses the Docker socket to launch paired jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent helper containers.

Config.Name: Appdata Directory
Config.Description: Persistent NanoClaw data: databases, logs, groups, channel state, env files, and host-visible runtime files for nested agent containers.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Required security-sensitive mount. NanoClaw v2 uses the Docker socket to spawn nested jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent helper containers, which grants host-level Docker control access.

Config.Name: Telegram Bot Token
Config.Description: Bot token from @BotFather. After startup, send the PAIR_TELEGRAM_CODE from the logs to this bot.

Config.Name: Anthropic API Key
Config.Description: Claude API key. Use this or one of the advanced Claude credential options.

Config.Name: Host Appdata Path
Config.Description: Host-side path matching the Appdata Directory mount. Nested agent containers need this host path when the AIO talks to the host Docker daemon.

Config.Name: Claude Code OAuth Token
Config.Description: Optional Claude Code OAuth-style credential. Use instead of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when applicable.

Config.Name: Anthropic Auth Token
Config.Description: Optional Claude/Anthropic auth token for runtimes that expect ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.

Config.Name: Anthropic Base URL
Config.Description: Optional Anthropic-compatible API endpoint override.

Config.Name: OneCLI URL
Config.Description: Optional OneCLI gateway URL for NanoClaw agent credential injection.

Config.Name: OneCLI API Key
Config.Description: Optional OneCLI API key.

Config.Name: Agent Image
Config.Description: Helper image used for spawned agent containers. Advanced users may point this to a custom built agent image.

Config.Name: Agent Image Base
Config.Description: Base repository NanoClaw uses when building per-agent customized helper images.

Config.Name: Container Timeout
Config.Description: Agent container timeout in milliseconds.

Config.Name: Idle Timeout
Config.Description: Idle timeout in milliseconds for keeping agent containers warm after results.

Config.Name: Max Output Size
Config.Description: Maximum captured output from an agent container in bytes.

Config.Name: Max Messages Per Prompt
Config.Description: Maximum message history items NanoClaw passes into a prompt.

Config.Name: Max Concurrent Containers
Config.Description: Maximum number of concurrent NanoClaw agent containers.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: NanoClaw log level.

Config.Name: Assistant Name
Config.Description: Assistant trigger name used by NanoClaw. Example trigger: @nanoclaw

Config.Name: Assistant Has Own Number
Config.Description: Set true only when your NanoClaw assistant has its own dedicated channel identity.

Config.Name: Auto Pair Telegram
Config.Description: When true, the container starts the pairing-code watcher on first boot.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone used by scheduled tasks and formatted timestamps.
